review_candidates.title: Director of business intelligence & automation (RPA & AI)
review_candidates.location: San Salvador, San Salvador, El Salvador
review_candidates.description: Build the automation layer that allows AI to operate inside real companies. MAIC is building the enterprise architecture for AI. Enterprises already have data, systems, processes, applications, documents, and people performing thousands of interconnected actions every day. The challenge is turning all of that into an environment where AI can understand what is happening and safely take action. That is where the Automation team comes in. MAIC connects enterprise systems and operational data into a shared context layer. On top of that context, we build workflows, automations, applications, and AI agents that help organizations operate faster, more intelligently, and with less manual work. As Director of Automation, you will lead the team responsible for turning enterprise context into execution. You will own the strategy, architecture, standards, and delivery of automation across MAIC — from traditional RPA and APIs to AI agents, human-in-the-loop workflows, and intelligent enterprise automation. This is not a traditional RPA leadership role. We are building the infrastructure that allows AI to interact with real business systems safely and reliably. What you will own You will own MAIC’s automation function end-to-end. That includes: * Automation strategy and technical direction. * Architecture for enterprise automations and workflows. * RPA and browser automation. * API-based integrations and system actions. * AI-powered and agentic workflows. * Human-in-the-loop approval systems. * Production reliability and monitoring. * Reusable automation components and connectors. * Automation engineering standards. * Team development and technical leadership. * Delivery of customer automation projects. * Identification of new opportunities for automation across customer operations. You will be responsible for determining not only how a process should be automated, but also which technology should automate it. Sometimes the answer will be an API. Sometimes it will be RPA. Sometimes it will be an AI agent. Sometimes it will be a deterministic workflow with human approval. And often, it will be a combination of all four. What would your day look like? * Lead and grow a team of RPA, automation, and AI engineers. * Design the architecture for complex enterprise automation projects. * Review customer processes and identify opportunities for automation, AI augmentation, and process redesign. * Translate operational requirements into scalable technical solutions. * Decide when to use APIs, RPA, workflow engines, agents, or human-in-the-loop execution. * Architect automations that span multiple enterprise systems and data sources. * Build standards for production-grade automation across MAIC deployments. * Ensure automations are observable, auditable, recoverable, and secure. * Establish patterns for retries, queues, idempotency, exception handling, logging, monitoring, and escalation. * Oversee browser and desktop automations for legacy systems where modern APIs are unavailable. * Design AI-powered workflows that can interpret emails, documents, messages, forms, and unstructured information. * Define how AI agents interact with enterprise systems and what actions they are allowed to perform. * Design approval and control mechanisms for sensitive actions. * Work closely with MAIC’s Enterprise AI, Product, Data, and Engineering teams. * Connect automation workflows to MAIC’s ontology and enterprise context layer. * Create reusable actions, integrations, connectors, and automation components that can be deployed across customers. * Review technical designs and code produced by the automation engineering team. * Mentor engineers and establish strong engineering practices. * Participate directly in critical customer implementations. * Own the reliability and performance of automation running in production. * Continuously evaluate new automation and agentic technologies and determine where they fit within MAIC’s architecture. The kind of problems you will solve A traditional automation might say: When an invoice arrives, enter these fields into the ERP. At MAIC, the problem might look more like: An invoice arrives by email. MAIC identifies the supplier, connects the invoice to the corresponding purchase order, validates the amount against the order, checks whether the goods were received, detects a discrepancy, identifies the employee responsible for the purchase, retrieves the relevant communication history, and determines that approval is required. An AI agent prepares the recommended action. A human approves it. The automation executes the appropriate action across the ERP and other systems. Everything is logged and auditable. That is the type of automation architecture you will help build. What do you need to be successful? * 7+ years of experience in software engineering, automation, RPA, systems integration, enterprise technology, or related fields. * Experience leading engineers or technical delivery teams. * Strong hands-on understanding of RPA and enterprise automation. * Experience with tools such as UiPath, Power Automate, Automation Anywhere, Robocorp, Playwright, Selenium, or similar technologies. * Strong software engineering fundamentals. * Experience with Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, Java, or similar languages. * Strong understanding of REST APIs, webhooks, authentication, databases, and enterprise integrations. * Experience designing integrations across complex enterprise systems. * Strong understanding of SQL and relational databases. * Experience designing distributed or asynchronous systems. * Understanding of queues, retries, idempotency, state management, and fault tolerance. * Experience operating automations or integrations in production environments. * Ability to design systems that are reliable, observable, secure, and maintainable. * Strong architectural judgment. * Ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and business leaders. * Experience working directly with customers or enterprise stakeholders. * Ability to understand complex business processes and translate them into technical architectures. * Strong leadership, mentoring, and problem-solving skills. Strong pluses * Experience building AI agents or LLM-powered applications. * Experience with tool calling, MCP, or agent orchestration. * Experience with intelligent document processing. * Experience with OCR, computer vision, or multimodal AI. * Experience with process mining. * Experience with workflow orchestration platforms. * Experience integrating SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics, Salesforce, ServiceNow, or similar enterprise platforms. * Experience with event-driven architectures. * Experience with cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP. * Experience with Kubernetes, Docker, or distributed systems. * Experience designing human-in-the-loop systems. * Understanding of enterprise identity, RBAC, permissions, security, and audit trails. * Familiarity with knowledge graphs, ontologies, or enterprise semantic models. Leadership expectations This role is not only about managing a team. You should be able to go deep technically when necessary. You should be comfortable reviewing an architecture in the morning, debugging a failed production automation in the afternoon, working through a customer’s operational process with their leadership team, and then helping an engineer design a better implementation. You will establish the engineering culture of the Automation team. We expect you to: * Set a high technical bar. * Build systems for reuse rather than one-off scripts. * Push the team toward API-first automation where appropriate. * Know when RPA is the right tool and when it is not. * Design automations for failure, not just the happy path. * Treat monitoring and observability as part of the product. * Build security and permissions into the architecture. * Keep humans in control of sensitive decisions. * Help engineers grow technically and professionally. * Turn lessons from individual customer implementations into reusable MAIC platform capabilities. Why this role matters AI can generate an answer. Enterprise AI needs to do much more. It needs to understand the organization, know what actions are possible, respect permissions and business rules, interact with existing systems, recover when something fails, and know when a human needs to make the final decision. MAIC’s context layer gives AI an understanding of the enterprise. The Automation team gives it the ability to act. As Director of Automation, you will build and lead that capability. By being part of MAIC You will work on the intersection of enterprise software, AI, automation, and real-world operations. You will build systems that interact with the core infrastructure companies use every day. You will lead engineers working across traditional automation, enterprise integrations, intelligent workflows, and AI agents. And you will help define what automation looks like in a world where software no longer just follows predefined steps — it can understand context and participate intelligently in business processes. You will lead the team responsible for turning enterprise AI from intelligence into action.
